title.en: Control of breathing and its disorders

summary.en: Breathing is normally an automatic, unconscious rhythm generated by respiratory centers in the brainstem, but the rate and depth of that rhythm are continuously adjusted by feedback from two distinct types of chemoreceptor monitoring the blood. Central chemoreceptors, located in the brainstem itself, respond primarily to carbon dioxide (technically, to the resulting change in cerebrospinal fluid pH) and provide the dominant, moment-to-moment drive to breathe under normal conditions -- a rising carbon dioxide level is a far more sensitive and immediate trigger to breathe more than a falling oxygen level is. Peripheral chemoreceptors, located in the carotid arteries and aorta, respond primarily to oxygen and only become the dominant drive to breathe when oxygen falls to a fairly low level, which is why the popular idea of oxygen as the main trigger for breathing gets the normal physiology backward. Sleep apnea, a common disorder of this control system, illustrates how the system can fail without any lung tissue disease at all: in obstructive sleep apnea, the problem is not the control system itself but the upper airway physically collapsing during sleep when muscle tone relaxes, repeatedly triggering brief arousals as chemoreceptor feedback detects the resulting rise in carbon dioxide, while in central sleep apnea, the brainstem's respiratory drive itself intermittently fails to signal a breath at all, a genuinely different mechanism producing a superficially similar pattern of interrupted breathing.
summary.et: Hingamine on normaalselt automaatne, teadvustamatu rütm, mida genereerivad ajutüve hingamiskeskused, kuid selle rütmi sagedust ja sügavust kohandatakse pidevalt tagasiside kaudu kahelt erinevalt kemoretseptori tüübilt, mis jälgivad verd. Kesksed kemoretseptorid, mis asuvad ajutüves endas, reageerivad peamiselt süsihappegaasile (täpsemalt sellest tulenevale ajuvedeliku pH muutusele) ja annavad domineeriva, hetkelise hingamistungi normaalsetes tingimustes -- tõusev süsihappegaasi tase on palju tundlikum ja vahetum hingamise stiimul kui langev hapnikutase. Perifeersed kemoretseptorid, mis asuvad unearterites ja aordis, reageerivad peamiselt hapnikule ja saavad domineerivaks hingamistungiks alles siis, kui hapnik langeb üsna madalale tasemele, mis ongi põhjus, miks populaarne idee hapnikust kui peamisest hingamise stiimulist pöörab normaalse füsioloogia ümber. Uneapnoe, selle kontrollisüsteemi levinud häire, illustreerib, kuidas süsteem võib ebaõnnestuda ilma igasuguse kopsukoe haiguseta: obstruktiivse uneapnoe puhul ei ole probleem kontrollisüsteem ise, vaid ülemiste hingamisteede füüsiline kokkukukkumine une ajal, kui lihastoonus lõõgastub, käivitades korduvalt lühikesed ärkamised, kui kemoretseptori tagasiside tuvastab sellest tuleneva süsihappegaasi tõusu, samas kui tsentraalse uneapnoe puhul ebaõnnestub ajutüve hingamistung ise vahepeal signaliseerimast hingetõmmet üldse, tõeliselt erinev mehhanism, mis tekitab pealtnäha sarnase katkendliku hingamise mustri.
